requirement: Evaluate an expression tree: arithmetic operators compute on numeric operands, comparison operators return a boolean, logical operators require boolean operands, a unary expression negates its boolean operand, a ternary expression requires a boolean condition and two branches of the same result type, and an invalid combination throws.

preconditions.text: The expression tree is built in memory from its operand and operator objects
The operands and operator produce a valid result type
The operand/operator combination is invalid or divides by zero

returns.text: Arithmetic expression evaluates to the expected numeric result
Comparison expression evaluates to the expected boolean result
Complex, unary, or ternary expression evaluates to the expected value
ArgumentException is thrown for mismatched operand types, an invalid operator for the type, a non-boolean condition, or division by zero

exception_text: ArgumentException is thrown when the operands or operator do not match the expression type, or when a division by zero is evaluated
